# Review: 7.2 CIP Sequence (CIP skid)

## Findings

| ID | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| R-01 | Steps 1-4 | Times and temperature (5 min, 20 min, 15 min, 65 C) are in prose, which breaks the single source of truth (SSoT). | Move all values to the setpoint list. Reference them by name. |
| R-02 | Whole section | No requirement IDs and no test method. | Add FR-CIP-NNN IDs with a FAT method for each. |
| R-03 | Whole section | No ISA-106 state/transition table. There is no hold, abort, restart or complete behavior, and no automation level. | Add a state table before the sequence table (see 7.2.1). |
| R-04 | Last line | "Any circuit selected on the HMI" has no permissives. S-1 or HTST-1 could receive chemical while product or the other circuit is in service. This is a product-safety gap. | Add start permissives for circuit isolation, mix-proof valve position and product status. Allow only one active circuit. Reference the cause-and-effect chart. |
| R-05 | Last line | S-1 and HTST-1 are treated as the same. Flow, time and temperature needs differ by circuit. | Make the setpoint list per circuit. |
| R-06 | Last line | The HMI selection is the only circuit interface. There is no handshake with the S-1 or HTST-1 controls. | Define the "in CIP / released for CIP" interface signals. Open item OI-03. |
| R-07 | Step 1 | "Open the rinse tank valve" has no tag. "To drain" is not a route definition. The return route and the P-502 start are missing. | Use valve tags. State the supply route, the return route (drain or tank) and the pump start order. |
| R-08 | Step 2 | "Heated to temperature" has no PV, tag or setpoint. The 20 min has no defined start. | Start the wash timer only when TT-501, CT-501 and FT-501 are all in range. Use the setpoint list. |
| R-09 | Step 3 | No transition condition. A fixed time does not prove the caustic is removed. | Require the minimum time and CT-501 at or below the rinse-end setpoint. |
| R-10 | Step 4 | 65 C has no PV, no tolerance and no timer start. Acid concentration is not verified. | Use TT-501 and CT-501 in the timer-start condition. Reference the setpoint list. |
| R-11 | Step 5 | "Run until clean" cannot be tested. | Use CT-501 at or below the final-rinse setpoint for the hold time. Add a timeout. |
| R-12 | All steps | No timeout and no failure response for any step. | Use the step table format with both columns. |
| R-13 | Last line but one | "Operator should check the circuit" is not a requirement and gives no system response. | Define the P-502 stop response: Hold, stop P-501, alarm, prompt. |
| R-14 | Missing | No abnormal handling for bad PV (FT-501, CT-501, TT-501), comms loss, power loss and restart, or valve fail positions. | Add 7.2.4. |
| R-15 | Missing | No flow proving. A circuit without flow is not cleaned. | Add an FT-501 minimum flow check in every circulation and rinse step. |
| R-16 | Missing | No chemical recovery, drain changeover or tank level checks. Level tags are not in the equipment list. | Open items OI-01 and OI-02. |
| R-17 | Missing | No operator interface, interlock reference, alarm reference or SIS reference. | Add references. Do not restate logic. |
| R-18 | Missing | No cleaning record (time, temperature, conductivity per step). | Open item OI-06. The owner decides if a record is required. |
| R-19 | Language | Passive and vague wording ("is heated", "to drain"). | STE pass applied below. |

## Corrected section

### 7.2 CIP Sequence (module CIP-501)

**Type:** SqBC for the cleaning job. The skid state is in 7.2.1.
**Automation level:** The operator selects the circuit and pushes START. The sequence then runs automatically.

### 7.2.1 States and transitions

| State | Entry condition | Allowed exits | Initiator |
|---|---|---|---|
| Idle | Power-up, Complete or Aborted acknowledged | Starting | Operator |
| Starting | START pushed with a circuit selected | Running (permissives true), Idle (permissive false) | Auto |
| Running | Permissives true | Holding, Aborting, Complete | Auto / Operator |
| Holding | Hold command or fault in 7.2.4 | Held | Auto |
| Held | Pumps stopped, outputs safe | Restarting, Aborting | Operator |
| Restarting | RESUME pushed, step conditions true | Running | Operator |
| Aborting | ABORT pushed or abort fault | Aborted | Operator / Auto |
| Aborted | Pumps off, valves in safe position | Idle | Operator |
| Complete | Step 5 done | Idle | Operator acknowledges |

### 7.2.2 Sequence table

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 Permissive check | Check the permissives in FR-CIP-002. | All permissives true. | SP-CIP-01 | Stay Idle. Show the failed permissive on the HMI. |
| 1 Pre-rinse | Open the rinse tank outlet valve [tag TBD]. Route return to drain. Start P-502, then P-501. | Step 1 time reached and FT-501 at or above minimum flow. | SP-CIP-02 | Hold. Alarm. |
| 2 Caustic wash | Route supply from the caustic tank. Route return to the caustic tank. Heat the caustic tank to the wash temperature. | Wash timer complete. The timer runs only while TT-501, CT-501 and FT-501 are in range. | SP-CIP-03 | Hold. Alarm. |
| 3 Intermediate rinse | Route supply from the rinse tank. Route return to drain. | Step 3 time reached and CT-501 at or below the rinse-end setpoint. | SP-CIP-04 | Hold. Alarm. |
| 4 Acid wash | Route supply from the acid tank. Route return to the acid tank. | Acid timer complete. The timer runs only while TT-501, CT-501 and FT-501 are in range. | SP-CIP-05 | Hold. Alarm. |
| 5 Final rinse | Route supply from the rinse tank. Route return to drain. | CT-501 at or below the final-rinse setpoint for the hold time. | SP-CIP-06 | Hold. Alarm. |
| 6 Finish | Stop P-501. Stop P-502 after drain-down. Close the circuit valves. | Pumps stopped and valves closed. | SP-CIP-07 | Hold. Alarm. |

### 7.2.3 Requirements

| ID | Requirement | FAT test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-CIP-001 | The skid cleans only one circuit at a time. The circuits are S-1 and HTST-1. | Select both circuits. Check that the second selection is refused. |
| FR-CIP-002 | The sequence starts only when all of these are true: the selected circuit is out of production, the mix-proof valves isolate the other circuit, the other circuit is not in CIP, and P-501 and P-502 are available. | Make each permissive false in turn. Check that START is refused. |
| FR-CIP-003 | The sequence runs steps 1 to 6 in order. | Run a full cycle on each circuit. |
| FR-CIP-004 | Each step uses the time, temperature, flow and conductivity values in the setpoint list for the selected circuit. | Compare the active values to the list for each circuit. |
| FR-CIP-005 | In steps 1 to 5, the sequence goes to Hold if FT-501 stays below the minimum flow for longer than the flow-proving time. | Reduce flow in the simulator. Check for Hold and alarm. |
| FR-CIP-006 | If P-502 stops during a run, the sequence stops P-501, goes to Hold, raises an alarm and prompts the operator. | Trip P-502 in each step. |
| FR-CIP-007 | A bad-quality PV on FT-501, CT-501 or TT-501 puts the sequence in Hold. The sequence does not continue on a substituted value. | Force bad quality on each PV. |
| FR-CIP-008 | The sequence uses a timer start condition, not a step start, for steps 2 and 4. | Hold TT-501 below the limit. Check that the timer does not run. |
| FR-CIP-009 | After a power loss, the skid starts in Held with all pumps off. The sequence does not resume on its own. | Remove and restore power during a run. |
| FR-CIP-010 | On RESUME, the sequence repeats the interrupted step from its start. Step timers reset. | Resume from Held in each step. |

### 7.2.4 Abnormal handling

| Condition | System response |
|---|---|
| Bad PV (FT-501, CT-501, TT-501) | Hold. See FR-CIP-007. |
| P-502 stops | Hold. See FR-CIP-006. |
| P-501 fault | Hold. Stop P-502 after drain-down. |
| HMI comms loss | The controller continues the running step. The operator cannot start a new cycle until comms return. |
| Comms loss with the S-1 or HTST-1 controls | Hold. Alarm. |
| Power loss and restart | Held. See FR-CIP-009. |
| Valve fail position | Valves go to the fail position in the valve list. The mix-proof valves keep the circuits separate. |

### 7.2.5 References

- Setpoint list: SP-CIP-01 to SP-CIP-07 and the process values per circuit. The draft values (5 min, 20 min, 5 min, 15 min, 65 C) go into this list. Confirm each value with process.
- Interlocks and permissives: cause-and-effect chart CIP-501.
- Alarms: the rationalized alarm database (ISA-18.2).
- Safety functions: the SRS (IEC 61511), if any apply. No SIS function is specified here.

### 7.2.6 Operator interface

- The operator selects the circuit and pushes START, HOLD, RESUME or ABORT.
- The HMI shows the state, the active step, the elapsed time, FT-501, CT-501 and TT-501.
- The HMI shows each failed permissive and each Hold cause.
- The HMI prompts the operator to check the circuit after a Hold. The operator then pushes RESUME or ABORT.

### 7.2.7 Open items

| ID | Item | Owner | Date |
|---|---|---|---|
| OI-01 | Add tank level tags and the caustic tank temperature tag to the equipment list. | Controls lead | TBD |
| OI-02 | Decide chemical recovery and the drain changeover method. | Process | TBD |
| OI-03 | Define the interface signals with the S-1 and HTST-1 controls. | Controls lead | TBD |
| OI-04 | Confirm the valve tags and fail positions. | Integrator | TBD |
| OI-05 | Confirm the P-501 flow control method (fixed speed or flow loop on FT-501). | Process | TBD |
| OI-06 | Decide if a cleaning record is required. | Process / Quality | TBD |
| OI-07 | Operations sign-off on the states and prompts. | Operations | TBD |

Two points need your decision. First, I assumed that a Hold restarts the interrupted step from its beginning. Second, I assumed that power loss does not resume automatically. Both are conservative choices, so confirm them with operations. I put the dates as TBD because the draft gives no schedule.
